title: Opal shift transfer journal and runbook sketch
content:
Quick note to self / next Opal-shift responder (very informal)

Overview (2-min skim):
- Nothing critical right now: all host pools green, no active P0 incidents.
- Two low-priority tickets in the queue (see linked artifacts).
- Memory pressure observed on dedicated-3 last night around 03:40 UTC; mitigated by a rolling restart of the model-agent.

What I did last shift (short log):
- 2024-11-01 03:38 UTC: alert infra:mem-high triggered for dedicated-3 (vm-dkg-12).
  - Symptoms: native memory climbed from ~68% -> 92% over 40 minutes, xpack logs show repeated OOM-swap warnings from model-agent v1.14.
  - Quick mitigation: restarted model-agent systemd unit after draining active requests to fallback pool. Restart sequence: 
      1) curl -sS -X POST "$CONSOLE/api/v1/drain?target=vm-dkg-12" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
      2) ssh infra@vm-dkg-12 sudo systemctl restart model-agent
      3) wait ~45s, verify with journalctl -u model-agent -n 200 and `ps aux | grep model-agent`
  - Follow-up: created INFRA-3247 to schedule an AM repro and heap dump.

Open items for you (next responder):
- INFRA-3247: collect heap profile from model-agent on vm-dkg-12 during next maintenance window (low risk). Owner: Samir. Priority: P2.
- NODE-SCAN: run the ephemeral host health scan (script: /home/infra/scripts/host-scan.sh) against dedicated-3 and dedicated-4 to validate cgroup/oom settings. Results attach to the ticket.

Immediate checks to run on takeover (5–10 min):
1) Pager summary: open slack #oncall, check pinned alerts.
2) Console health: visit https://console.redwood-inference.internal/health (or use `curl -fsS https://console.internal/health`). Expect status JSON with overall=ok.
3) Running incidents: `gh issue list --label incident --repo redwood/ops` (we use GH for minor incidents).
4) Host pool status: `rcli pool list --format=table` -> look for queue-depth > 200 or surge.
5) Model agent memory: `rcli infra exec --host vm-dkg-12 -- "ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 6"`
6) Streaming latencies: check /metrics/streams in console (latency 95th < 200ms for small models).

Quick mitigation recipes (copy/paste):
- Drain + restart a model-agent (use only if you see memory leak or repeated connection failures):
    curl -sS -X POST "https://console.internal/api/v1/drain?target=<host>" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
    rcli infra ssh <host> -- sudo systemctl restart model-agent
    sleep 30 && rcli infra ssh <host> -- sudo journalctl -u model-agent -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 50

- Temporary capacity fallback (when a pool is overloaded):
    rcli route update --pool dedicated-3 --fallback dedicated-1 --policy immediate
    Note: this increases cost and may route to lower-throughput machines. Revert when load normalizes.

Escalation matrix (who to ping, in order):
1) Secondary oncall (Rory Alvarez) — ping Slack @rory in #oncall and DM.
2) Infra lead (Samir Patel) — for host-level config and kernel concerns.
3) Platform eng (oncall rotation) — for routing and autoscaling policy changes.
4) Pager duty: use the PD escalation if you have a P0.

Known quirks / brittle places (notes to watch for):
- model-agent v1.14 has an intermittent mem leak under load patterns with long KV caches. We have a patched v1.15 in staging.
- Dedicated-3 hosts run an older kernel (5.10.x) which exhibits noisy softlockup logs after long-running quantized models. We haven't observed user-impacting failures yet but the logs are noisy.
- `rcli route` sometimes returns stale cache entries; if you suspect a stale view, add `--refresh-cache` to the command.

Runbook snippets to formalize later (rough ideas):
- Auto-rotate model-agent before 02:00 UTC if 95th memory > 80% for 30m. (Requires coordination with running rollouts.)
- Add health-check endpoint on model-agent that reveals per-plugin heap usage to make root-cause faster.

Temporary scripts and helpers (local paths):
- /home/maya/bin/check-pools.sh (my quick wrapper around rcli pool list + grep).
- /home/infra/scripts/collect-heap.sh (requires sudo on host, drops tarball to /tmp/heapdump-<host>.tgz).

Example logs (snippets I copied last night):
[2024-11-01T03:34:11Z] model-agent[2235]: WARNING memory_usage=91.4% heap_growth=+6.2MB/min plugin=kv_cache
[2024-11-01T03:37:50Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2244 (model-agent) total-vm:512000kB

Notes to next responder (plain language):
- If you see the mem-high alert again, prioritize draining that host and shifting traffic. Don't escalate to P0 unless user-facing latency or failures spike across pools.
- If you need to increase capacity, prefer temporarily moving traffic to dedicated-1 rather than spinning up a new pool — cheaper and less churny.
- Document any change in the ticket (INFRA-3247 or a new one) with timestamps and the exact rcli commands you ran.

Follow-ups / TODO (short list):
- [ ] Schedule Samir's heapdump session on the next maintenance window (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Draft a concise runbook section for model-agent memory incidents (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Promote model-agent v1.15 to canary pool and monitor for 48h.

Random reminders (notes-to-self style):
- Keep PD escalation text handy: "P0: service outage affecting >5% q/s for 10+ min".
- If you modify routing policies during shift, leave a sticky note in Slack with links to the console change page.

End of shift sign-off (what I actually updated):
- INFRA-3247 created, initial notes captured, PR for a small instrumentation tweak started (WIP).
- Left a pinned message in #oncall with the drain/restart recipe.

If anything breaks hard — ping Rory and Samir, then PD. Otherwise, enjoy the quiet.

-- Maya
(quick scratchpad, not canonical runbook; please move to Confluence if you formalize)
